clue.text: Get shot of welcoming resort in post

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in a guest, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: to get shot of something is to ditch it
a spa is a resort town with mineral springs

explanation.surface: Someone wants to get rid of the holiday spot that has been advertised in the mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get shot of' reads like the definition, but it is wordplay; 'post' as a verb is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To post a letter is to send it off, a synonym of the verb for sending.

clue.text: Intended to put on thinking cap

definitions.meaning: something intended is done on purpose, the adjective sense
to put on one's thinking cap is to ponder carefully, the verb sense

explanation.surface: Someone meant to start thinking hard.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means done on purpose, and the verb means to consider carefully; one spelling covers both.

clue.text: See rabbit, climbing, fall

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to rabbit is British slang for chattering on, as is to gas

explanation.surface: A warning to watch a rabbit scrambling up and then tumbling down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is only a link here. 'Rabbit' (from rhyming slang 'rabbit and pork' = talk) means chatter, like 'gas'.
explanation.definitionFit: To sag is to droop or sink down, a near synonym of falling.

clue.text: Previously willing to support a Labour leader

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below the pieces it holds up
the leader of a word is its first letter, here that of Labour

parts.note: willing and ready both mean prepared to do something

explanation.surface: Someone was formerly happy to back a Labour Party leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour is the British left-of-centre party.
explanation.definitionFit: Already means by an earlier time, which is what previously expresses.

clue.text: Bats hit hard repeatedly

parts.note: to crack someone is to hit them hard
to brain someone is to hit them hard on the head; 'repeatedly' says the phrase supplies two words

explanation.surface: A cricket or baseball player strikes the ball forcefully again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bats' looks like sports equipment but is the slang adjective meaning crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Bats is slang for mad, and crackbrained describes someone foolish or crazy in the same informal register.

clue.text: Right backs without any caps

indicators.note: backs here is a verb meaning goes backwards, so the phrase is read in reverse

parts.note: without any caps means having no tops, so no + tops

explanation.surface: A sports report says the correct defenders have never been capped for their country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backs' and 'caps' suggest football or rugby defenders and international appearances.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot on is informal for exactly correct, a synonym of right in that sense.

clue.text: Indian possibly shot in quiet university

parts.note: p, for piano, is the musical abbreviation for quiet

indicators.note: in means the shot is placed inside the other letters

parts.note: uni is the informal short form of university
a jab is a shot, an injection

explanation.surface: An Indian student may have been given a vaccination at a peaceful college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' suggests gunfire but means an injection, a jab.
explanation.definitionFit: A Punjabi comes from the Punjab region, so may be Indian; 'possibly' marks it as an example.

clue.text: Stealing without a single thought — that's preposterous!

indicators.note: without means the single letter is removed from the word for stealing

parts.note: stealing is thievery
I is the Roman numeral for one, a single
a thought is an idea

explanation.surface: A thief who acts without thinking at all is behaving absurdly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes I out of THIEVERY, leaving THEVERY.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an exclamation of indignant disbelief at an outrageous suggestion.

clue.text: When school's over, record a piece of music, too

definitions.text: record a piece of music, too

indicators.note: over in a down clue means turned upside down, so read in reverse

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: After term ends, someone also writes down a musical composition.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is double: 'record' (to jot down) and 'a piece of music' (a single tone), the 'too' marking the second.
explanation.definitionFit: To write down is one sense, and a single musical tone is another sense of the same short word.

clue.text: Cricket ball split by Lancashire opener, say

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter, here that of Lancashire

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated eg
to split is to break

explanation.surface: A Lancashire opening batsman, for example, is split up by a cricket ball.
explanation.walkthrough: A leg break is a delivery in cricket that spins from the leg side towards the off side; Lancashire is an English county side.
explanation.definitionFit: A leg break is a type of spin bowling delivery in cricket, so a kind of ball bowled.

clue.text: Trendy wine set

parts.note: in means fashionable, trendy
tent is a deep red Spanish wine

explanation.surface: A fashionable wine collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' looks like a noun for a group, but it is the adjective meaning determined, as in 'set on winning'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being intent on something means being resolved to do it, just as being set on it does.

clue.text: Press run rackets in such a tournament

parts.note: to press is to squash
a run in a stocking is called a ladder in Britain

explanation.surface: Journalists describe a racket sport event with a pressing schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: A ladder in tights is the British term for what Americans call a run.
explanation.definitionFit: A squash ladder is a ranking competition among squash players, and squash is played with rackets.

clue.text: Where men may be trained to jeer a conservative

parts.note: to barrack is British for to jeer or heckle
a square is an old-fashioned, conventional person

explanation.surface: A place where men might be taught to heckle a Tory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conservative' suggests a political party, but here it is a staid, conventional person, a square.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrack square is the parade ground where soldiers drill and train.

clue.text: Urchins spoiling funfair games, short of energy

indicators.note: spoiling suggests ruining, so the letters are wrecked and rearranged
short of means lacking, so one letter is dropped

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Street children ruin the fairground attractions when they run out of steam.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove E from FUNFAIRGAMES, then 'spoiling' rearranges the remaining eleven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragamuffin is a scruffy, ragged child, the same as a street urchin.

clue.text: Failing to give wife her stout

indicators.note: failing suggests breaking down, so the letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A husband fails to hand over his porter to his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stout' looks like the dark beer but is the adjective meaning fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Stout describes a heavily built person, carrying too much weight.

clue.text: Cover close in game

parts.note: a rug is a covering for a floor or a person
by means near, close at hand

explanation.surface: A rug sits nearby during a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugby is a ball sport, an example of a game.

clue.text: Broadcast of extremely trivial variety?

indicators.note: broadcast also means scattered widely, so these letters are strewn into a new order
extremely points to the extremes, the first and last letters of trivial

explanation.surface: A sniffy description of a kind of television programme full of trivia.
explanation.walkthrough: Take TL, the ends of 'trivial', and add VARIETY; 'Broadcast' scatters them.
explanation.definitionFit: Reality television shows ordinary people in unscripted situations, often thought trivial viewing.

clue.text: Confusing my boot with his, like George in The Famous Five?

definitions.text: like George in The Famous Five?

indicators.note: confusing means mixing up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone mixes up their boot with a boy's, behaving like a character from a children's adventure series.
explanation.walkthrough: George (Georgina) is the girl who acts like a boy in Enid Blyton's Famous Five children's books.
explanation.definitionFit: George insists on being treated as a boy, so she behaves in a boyish girl's manner.

clue.text: Collection of writings found in vehicle

definitions.meaning: a volume gathering several works by one author
the old full name for a bus

explanation.surface: An anthology turns up on a bus.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a book of collected works and also, in its old form, a public bus.

clue.text: Badminton competitor's qualification

definitions.meaning: Badminton is a famous English horse trials event, so a competitor is a horseman
a clause added to qualify a statement or a bill

explanation.surface: A shuttlecock player's credentials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badminton' suggests the racket game, but it is the horse trials held at Badminton House in England.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a person on horseback; the other is a clause added to a document as a proviso.

clue.text: Scrub computer key inside protective covering

indicators.note: inside means the key goes within the covering

parts.note: a rind is the tough outer skin of fruit or cheese
Esc is the escape key on a keyboard

explanation.surface: Someone cleans a keyboard key inside its case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrub' looks like cleaning but is the informal sense of cancel.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrub a plan is informal for cancelling it, as to rescind is to revoke.

clue.text: Western fan seeking an unusual book title

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cowboy-film enthusiast hunts for an odd name for a book.
explanation.walkthrough: Finnegans Wake is James Joyce's famously difficult final novel.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the title of James Joyce's last novel, so a book title.

clue.text: Finish off learning card game

indicators.note: to finish off here is to cut off the final letter

parts.note: study is learning

explanation.surface: Someone completes their studies with a game of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: Stud is a form of poker.
explanation.definitionFit: Stud poker is a well-known card game in which some cards are dealt face up.

clue.text: One pound cut in tax? That's novel

indicators.note: cut in means the pieces are inserted into the word for tax

parts.note: to tax someone's patience is to try it
I is the Roman numeral one
lb is the abbreviation for a pound weight

explanation.surface: A tax rise of a pound strikes someone as something new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective meaning new, but it is the noun: George du Maurier's novel Trilby, home of Svengali.
explanation.definitionFit: Trilby is an 1894 novel by George du Maurier, so it is an example of a novel.

clue.text: Approving of demo, oddly enough, during broadcast

indicators.note: during means the odd letters sit within the word for broadcast

parts.note: an airing is a broadcast

indicators.note: oddly takes the odd-numbered letters of demo

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys a demonstration, strangely, while it is being shown on air.
explanation.definitionFit: Admiring something means regarding it with approval, so the participle matches approving of.

clue.text: American concealing mounting fury

indicators.note: mounting in a down clue means going up, so the letters are read backwards
concealing means the word American holds the letters within it

explanation.surface: An American keeps a rising rage under wraps.
explanation.definitionFit: Ire is a literary word for anger, the same as fury.

clue.text: Neglect two girls, having borne son

parts.note: Di is a short girl's name

indicators.note: having borne means carrying a child within, so the son goes inside

parts.note: Sue is another short girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone ignores two young women after they have given birth to a boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Disuse is the state of being no longer used, as a neglected thing is.

clue.text: Inclination of general, say, about to lose power

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the general's name goes round the other piece

parts.note: Ulysses S. Grant was a US Civil War general; 'say' marks him as an example
an engine or battery is said to die when it loses power

explanation.surface: A general's tendency, for example, to be about to lose his authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads as a phrase meaning soon, but 'about' is the container and 'to lose power' is DIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A gradient is a slope, and an inclination is a slope or incline.
